primary_source.title: What is Missing from AI Post-Training AI: An Empirical Analysis

verified_observations: The observational corpus contains 1,338 public PostTrainBench trajectories across seven benchmarks, four base models, five agent interfaces and 20 agent-model configurations; 900 trajectories launch at least one model update.

The main conservative strategy annotator recognizes 3,557 adjacent training pairs and labels 74 as a coarse strategy change: 35 objective-family, 38 data-source and 1 stage-structure change, or 2.08%. The 74 changes come from 44 trajectories.
Initial-strategy defaults match the worker: Claude Code anchors on full SFT in 163/202 recognized cases (80.7%); Codex CLI anchors on PEFT in 268/299 (89.6%).

In the controlled Qwen3-1.7B-Base intervention, each configuration has three independent runs. Opus 4.6 autonomous scores 64.70% on GSM8K and 22.00% on HumanEval; the experience-driven framework scores 77.30% and 62.80%, matching +12.6 and +40.8 percentage-point improvements.

The paper reports that the experience/evaluator machinery improves execution but does not induce the recommended high-level strategy switch; its HumanEval trace remains in repeated SFT variants despite strategy-level advice.

On AIME 2025 the richer framework spends 7.9x the baseline tokens and about 66.7M tokens for one additional problem solved in its best run; the paper explicitly says that difference lies within evaluation variance.

The human-guidance intervention can redirect the initial strategy, but tests only guidance before execution; after training begins the representative guided trajectory returns to local optimization rather than autonomous strategy reopening.

scope_corrections.correction: The 2.1% statistic is conditional on 3,557 recognized adjacent pairs under a deliberately coarse strategy representation, not all possible semantic strategy changes. The paper states data-source changes are lower-bound observations. Therefore 97.9% must not be read as a proven rate of 'no meaningful strategy revision' over every adjacent experiment pair.

The 1,338-trajectory corpus is observational. Agent model, prompt, interface and scaffold are not independently randomized, and the authors explicitly say these effects cannot be separated. Default-strategy differences therefore diagnose recurring lock-in patterns rather than causal scaffold/model effects.

The experience-driven condition is a bundle (journal, skill library, evaluator agent and additional inference/evaluation activity) and consumes materially more tokens. Its score gain is evidence of better execution under the bundle, not an isolated causal effect of persistent memory or evaluator feedback.

AIME human-guidance and compute-scaling results do not establish a reliable performance effect: the paper itself places the one-problem difference within evaluation variance. Their strongest evidence is behavioral—external guidance can change the initial plan, while spontaneous later reopening remains absent in the observed traces.
The paper diagnoses a missing spontaneous strategy-reopening mechanism; it does not test a specific autonomous reopen/switch/retire controller that causally improves final performance.

assessment.supported_claim: Across the stated PostTrainBench corpus and controlled follow-ups, agents frequently perform strong local post-training execution while rarely making coarse high-level strategy changes after execution begins; more experience/guidance/compute does not by itself demonstrate spontaneous strategy reopening.
not_supported: Only exactly 2.1% of all meaningful strategic decisions change in the population of AI research agents.
A particular model or scaffold causally creates strategy lock-in in the observational corpus.
The richer framework's performance gain is attributable to one isolated memory/evaluator component.
A tested autonomous strategy-reopening controller is already shown to improve scientific or post-training outcomes.
